content.thinking: I notice these same coordinates (78, 72, 222, 239, 311, 35, 273, 356) keep showing up, suggesting they might be privileged outlier dimensions. I want to check the weights and biases for these dims, and see if they're also large in other weight matrices, since this resembles the "massive activation" phenomenon seen in outlier residual stream features. If a few dims dominate the residual stream magnitude, that could explain why LayerNorm output concentrates on them.

import numpy as np
dims=[78,72,222,239,311,35,273,356,300,162,223,60,136,114,360]
print('dim  ln1w0  ln1b0  ln2w0  ln2b0 ln1w1 ln1b1 ln1w2 ln1b2 ln1w3 ln1b3 | rownorm Wo0 Wp0 Wo1 Wp1 | colnorm q0 k0 v0 fc0')
for d in dims:
    print(d, ' '.join(f"{W[n][d]:6.2f}" for n in ['ln1_w.0','ln1_b.0','ln2_w.0','ln2_b.0','ln1_w.1','ln1_b.1','ln1_w.2','ln1_b.2','ln1_w.3','ln1_b.3']),'|',
          ' '.join(f"{np.linalg.norm(W[n][d]):5.2f}" for n in ['W_o.0','W_proj.0','W_o.1','W_proj.1']),'|',
          ' '.join(f"{np.linalg.norm(W[n][:,d]):5.2f}" for n in ['W_q.0','W_k.0','W_v.0','W_fc.0']))
